questions.prompt: What is a job?
choices: Work you do to earn money
A game you play for fun
questions.explanation: A job is work people do, and they get paid money for it.

questions.prompt: Which of these is a job?
questions.explanation: Teachers do work and get paid. That's a job!

questions.prompt: People get paid money for doing their jobs.
questions.explanation: True! Getting paid is called earning.

questions.prompt: You rake leaves for ${p} per yard. You rake {n} yards. How much do you earn?
questions.explanation: ${p} × {n} = ${ANSWER}.

questions.prompt: Why do some jobs pay more than others?
choices: They need special skills or training
questions.explanation: Jobs that need lots of skill, training or responsibility usually pay more.

questions.prompt: Getting a better job title and more pay at work is called a…
questions.explanation: A promotion is when you move up at work, often with more pay!

questions.prompt: You earn ${r} an hour at a bakery. How much do you earn in {h} hours?
questions.explanation: ${r} × {h} hours = ${ANSWER}.

questions.prompt: You could babysit for $20 or go to a party. What is the 'trade-off' if you choose the party?
questions.explanation: Every choice gives something up. Going to the party means giving up the $20 you could have earned.

questions.prompt: What's a good way to earn more money in the future?
questions.explanation: Learning skills helps you get better jobs that pay more.

questions.prompt: You mow {n} lawns for ${p} each, but the gas for the mower costs ${g}. How much do you keep?
questions.explanation: {n} × ${p} = earnings. Then subtract ${g} for gas: ${ANSWER}.

questions.prompt: Asking politely for fair pay, using facts, is called…
questions.explanation: Negotiating means talking to agree on a fair deal.

questions.prompt: Who collects taxes?
questions.explanation: Governments collect taxes to pay for things everyone uses.

questions.prompt: Your paycheck says you earned $100 but you took home $88. Where did $12 go?
questions.explanation: Taxes are taken out of paychecks. That's why take-home pay is less.

questions.prompt: Money you earn BEFORE taxes are taken out is called…
questions.explanation: Gross pay is the full amount before taxes. Net pay is what you take home.

questions.prompt: You earned ${g}. Taxes took ${t}. What is your take-home (net) pay?
questions.explanation: Net pay = gross − taxes = ${g} − ${t} = ${ANSWER}.

questions.prompt: Taxes help pay for firefighters and public schools.
questions.explanation: True! Taxes pay for services everyone shares.

questions.prompt: A $20 toy has a 5% sales tax. How much is the tax?
Which is safe to share with a stranger online?
questions.explanation: Fun facts are okay. Never share passwords, addresses or card numbers.

questions.prompt: If a message says you won a prize and asks for your password, it's probably a trick.
questions.explanation: True! Real prizes never need your password.

questions.prompt: A game player says 'give me your login and I'll give you free coins.' What do you do?
choices: Say no and tell a grown-up
questions.explanation: That's a trick to steal your account. Never share your login!

questions.prompt: Which password is strongest?
questions.explanation: Long passwords made of several random words are much harder to guess.

questions.prompt: Someone online says 'Keep our chat a secret from your parents.' That is…
choices: A warning sign, tell a trusted adult
questions.explanation: People who ask you to keep secrets from your family online are being unsafe. Tell an adult.

questions.prompt: What should you do before buying something online?
choices: Ask a grown-up to check the website
Type in any card you find
questions.explanation: A grown-up can help check that a store is real and safe.

questions.prompt: A message is full of spelling mistakes and says 'HURRY OR LOSE YOUR ACCOUNT!!!' It is most likely…
questions.explanation: Rushing you, scary threats and lots of mistakes are signs of a scam.

questions.prompt: Why shouldn't you use the same password for everything?
choices: If one gets stolen, all your accounts are at risk
questions.explanation: If a thief gets one password, they try it everywhere. Different passwords keep the others safe.

questions.prompt: Which is a NEED?
questions.explanation: A toothbrush keeps you healthy. That's a need!

questions.prompt: Which is a WANT?
questions.explanation: Ice cream is a yummy treat, a want.

questions.prompt: You have $5. You need lunch ($4) and want a comic ($3). What should you buy?
questions.explanation: Buy the need first. You can save up for the comic later.

questions.prompt: Shoes are a need. Which shoes are a 'need' choice instead of a 'want' choice?
choices: Shoes with a famous logo, for $90
questions.explanation: Good, simple shoes meet the need. Paying extra for logos or lights is the 'want' part.

questions.prompt: A want can never be part of a good budget.
questions.explanation: False! Wants are fine in a budget, just plan for them after needs and saving.

questions.prompt: You earn ${e}. You save half. How much do you save?
questions.explanation: Half of ${e} is ${ANSWER}.

questions.prompt: Your paycheck is ${p}. You spend ${a} on a game and ${b} on snacks. How much is left?
Why do people make a budget?
choices: To plan their money so they don't run out
questions.explanation: A budget is a plan that helps make sure there's money for needs, wants and savings.

questions.prompt: Starting your own lemonade stand is an example of…
questions.explanation: When you sell something yourself, you're running a business!

questions.prompt: What is a paycheck?
choices: The money your job pays you
questions.explanation: A paycheck is the money you get for working.

questions.prompt: You get paid ${w} each week. How much in {n} weeks?
questions.explanation: ${w} × {n} = ${ANSWER}.

questions.prompt: You earn ${r}/hour. Your boss gives you a $1/hour raise. How much more will you earn in a {h}-hour week?
questions.explanation: An extra $1 × {h} hours = ${ANSWER} more each week.

questions.prompt: What's the safest way to check a message that says it's from your bank?
choices: Ask a grown-up to call the bank's real phone number
Click the link in the message
questions.explanation: Contact the bank yourself using a number or website you already know is real.

questions.prompt: Lots of people want to buy the new SuperBall, but stores only have a few. What happens to the price?
choices: It stays exactly the same forever
questions.explanation: When many people want something rare, the price usually goes up.

questions.prompt: Technology companies make things like apps and computers. What do they need to make them?
questions.explanation: Skilled workers, like coders and designers, build technology. That's why those skills are valuable.

questions.prompt: Which helper earns money?
choices: A dog walker paid by neighbors
questions.explanation: The dog walker is doing a job and getting paid.

questions.prompt: Some of the money from a paycheck goes to taxes.
questions.explanation: True! Taxes come out of paychecks.

questions.prompt: Your PIN is like a…
choices: Secret password for your bank card
questions.explanation: A PIN is a secret number. Keep it secret!

questions.prompt: Which is the best example of a 'need' that some people turn into a 'want'?
choices: Buying a fancy $8 coffee instead of water
questions.explanation: Everyone needs drinks, but an expensive coffee is the 'want' version.

questions.prompt: A worker who always shows up on time and works hard is called…
questions.explanation: Reliable workers are trusted, and often promoted!

questions.prompt: Coders, nurses and electricians all need…
choices: To be grown-ups only for one day
questions.explanation: Most good jobs take training and practice to learn the skills.

questions.prompt: You got $10 for your birthday. What is a SMART plan?
choices: Save some, spend some, share some
Give it all to a stranger online
questions.explanation: Splitting money into save, spend and share is a great plan!

questions.prompt: Identity theft is when someone…
choices: Pretends to be you using your information
questions.explanation: Thieves use stolen info like names, birthdays and passwords to pretend to be someone else. Keep your info private!

questions.prompt: Job A pays $12/hour for 10 hours. Job B pays $100 for the same week. How much MORE does Job A pay?
Why might a person get some tax money back (a refund)?
choices: Too much tax was taken from their paychecks
questions.explanation: If more tax was taken out than needed, the government gives the extra back.

questions.prompt: You sell {n} cookies for ${p} each. How much money do you make?
questions.explanation: {n} × ${p} = ${ANSWER}.

questions.prompt: It's safe to click any link a stranger sends you.
questions.explanation: False! Strange links can be tricks. Ask a grown-up first.
